meta.scalability_note: 2 German regions (Cologne, Hamburg), managed K8s auto-scaling, no serverless FaaS; limited global footprint restricts horizontal scale-out beyond DACH
meta.performance_note: BSI C5 attested, ISO 27001 certified, 99.95% SLA, all data centers located in Germany; high compliance assurance with strong uptime guarantee

AWS Amplify.note: No managed frontend or full-stack web application hosting platform. Web apps must be self-hosted on VMs or Kubernetes.

AWS Lambda.note: No Function-as-a-Service offering. Serverless compute is not part of the PlusServer portfolio; workloads require VMs or containers.

Amazon ECS.note: No managed container runtime service outside of Kubernetes. Container orchestration is only available via PSKE (managed K8s).

Amazon EKS.note: Fully managed Kubernetes service with auto-scaling, GitOps-ready configuration, and multi-version support. Available in both German regions.

Amazon EC2.note: Flexible VM instances across multiple flavor profiles (general purpose, compute-optimized, memory-optimized). OpenStack Nova backend.

AWS Batch.note: No managed batch compute service. Batch workloads must be orchestrated manually via VMs or Kubernetes Jobs.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No PaaS application deployment platform. Application lifecycle management requires custom pipelines.

Amazon S3.note: Multi-region S3-compatible object storage with full S3 API support. Hosted exclusively in German data centers.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: No archival or cold-storage tier. Object Storage is offered at a single standard tier with no automated lifecycle archival.

Amazon EBS.note: SSD and NVMe-backed block volumes attachable to compute instances. Snapshots supported. Managed via OpenStack Cinder.

AWS Backup.note: VM snapshots and volume snapshots are available for manual and scheduled use. No centralised cross-service backup orchestration or policy engine.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed shared or distributed file system. NFS can be self-hosted on compute instances but is not offered as a managed service.

Amazon RDS.note: Managed PostgreSQL and MySQL with automated backups, point-in-time recovery, and high-availability failover.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: No managed document database service. MongoDB or similar must be self-hosted.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed NoSQL key-value or wide-column database service.

Amazon Aurora.note: No high-performance distributed relational database equivalent to Aurora.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: Managed Redis instance available. Clustering options are limited and Redis Cluster mode with advanced sharding is not fully supported.

Amazon Redshift.note: No managed cloud data warehouse service.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: HTTP/HTTPS load balancing with TLS termination, health checks, and routing rules. Managed via OpenStack Octavia.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP-level load balancing is available via the same Octavia product. Advanced NLB features such as static IPs and ultra-low latency modes are limited.

Amazon VPC.note: Full private networking with subnets, routing tables, security groups, and floating IPs. Managed via OpenStack Neutron.

Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS service with support for all standard record types. Managed via OpenStack Designate.

Amazon API Gateway.note: No managed API gateway service. API management requires self-hosted solutions such as Kong or nginx.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No global CDN service. Content delivery requires third-party CDN integration.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Dedicated private connectivity to PlusServer data centers is available on request. Limited self-service provisioning; requires manual engagement.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image/video analysis service.

Amazon SageMaker.note: No managed machine learning platform for model training and deployment.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed generative AI or foundation model API service.

AWS Glue.note: No managed ETL or serverless data integration service.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data processing service (Hadoop/Spark). Must be self-hosted.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless interactive query service for data in object storage.

AWS IAM.note: Full RBAC with support for projects, domains, roles, and federated identity. Managed via OpenStack Keystone.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed user identity and authentication service for applications. Requires self-hosted identity providers (e.g. Keycloak).

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No centralized SSO or workforce identity management service.

AWS KMS.note: Key lifecycle management available via OpenStack Barbican. HSM integration is limited and not offered as a standard self-service feature.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: No managed secrets rotation and storage service. Secrets management requires self-hosted tools such as HashiCorp Vault.

AWS Certificate Manager.equivalent: TLS Certificate Provisioning via Load Balancer
AWS Certificate Manager.note: TLS certificate provisioning is handled via the load balancer with Let's Encrypt integration. No standalone managed certificate lifecycle service.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: No managed threat detection or continuous security monitoring service.

AWS Security Hub.note: No managed cloud security posture management or centralised finding aggregation service.

AWS Config.note: No managed resource configuration tracking or compliance evaluation service.

AWS Shield.note: Network-level DDoS mitigation is provided at the data center perimeter. No advanced application-layer or WAF-integrated DDoS mitigation.

AWS WAF.note: Basic web application firewall available. Rule customisation is limited compared to AWS WAF managed rule groups.

AWS CloudTrail.note: IAM and API activity audit logging via OpenStack Keystone. Log retention periods and export options are limited.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Prometheus and Grafana-based metrics collection and alerting are provided. Less tightly integrated with platform services than CloudWatch.

Amazon SNS.note: No managed pub/sub or push notification service.

AWS Systems Manager.note: No managed operational tooling for patching, run commands, or inventory collection.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed billing dashboard with per-resource cost breakdown and usage history. Available in the customer portal.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI build service. CI pipelines require self-hosted or third-party tools (e.g. GitLab CI, Jenkins).

AWS CodeDeploy.note: No managed application deployment automation service.

AWS CodePipeline.note: No managed CI/CD pipeline orchestration service.

Amazon ECR.note: Managed OCI/Docker container registry with namespace isolation. Integrated with PSKE for image pulls.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native infrastructure-as-code service. An official Terraform provider is available for PlusServer OpenStack resources.

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT connectivity or device messaging platform.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device registry or fleet management service.

Amazon SQS.note: No managed message queue service. Message queuing requires self-hosted solutions such as RabbitMQ or Kafka.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus or event-driven integration service.

AWS Step Functions.note: No managed serverless workflow orchestration service.

Amazon SES.note: No managed transactional or bulk email delivery service.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming or ingestion service.
